bottom_line: In patients with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation, rivaroxaban was noninferior to warfarin for stroke or systemic embolism (hazard ratio in the rivaroxaban group, 0.79; 95% CI, 0.66 to 0.96).
implications: These results support that rivaroxaban achieved noninferiority versus warfarin for stroke/systemic embolism in this moderate-to-high-risk nonvalvular atrial fibrillation population (per-protocol HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.66 to 0.96; intention-to-treat HR 0.88, 95% CI 0.74 to 1.03), while major and nonmajor clinically relevant bleeding was similar (HR 1.03, 95% CI 0.96 to 1.11) and intracranial hemorrhage (0.5% vs. 0.7% per year) and fatal bleeding (0.2% vs. 0.5% per year) were lower with rivaroxaban; the intention-to-treat superiority test for the primary endpoint was not significant (P = 0.12).

major_points.text: Randomized, double-blind trial in 14,264 patients with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation at increased stroke risk, comparing once-daily rivaroxaban with dose-adjusted warfarin.
major_points.quote: In a double-blind trial, we randomly assigned 14,264 patients with nonvalvular atrial fibril- lation who were at increased risk for stroke to receive either rivaroxaban (at a daily dose of 20 mg) or dose-adjusted warfarin.

major_points.text: Primary efficacy endpoint was the composite of stroke (ischemic or hemorrhagic) and systemic embolism.
major_points.quote: The primary efficacy end point was the compos- ite of stroke (ischemic or hemorrhagic) and sys- temic embolism.

major_points.text: Per-protocol as-treated primary analysis met noninferiority with lower event rate for rivaroxaban vs warfarin.
major_points.quote: the primary end point occurred in 188 patients in the riva- roxaban group (1.7% per year) and in 241 in the warfarin group (2.2% per year) (hazard ratio in the rivaroxaban group, 0.79; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.66 to 0.96;

major_points.text: Intention-to-treat analysis also met noninferiority, but not superiority.
major_points.quote: In the intention-to-treat analysis, the primary end point occurred in 269 patients in the rivaroxaban group (2.1% per year) and in 306 patients in the warfarin group (2.4% per year) (hazard ratio, 0.88; 95% CI, 0.74 to 1.03; P<0.001 for noninferiority; P = 0.12 for superiority).

major_points.text: Principal safety endpoint (major and nonmajor clinically relevant bleeding) was similar between groups.
major_points.quote: Major and nonmajor clinically rel- evant bleeding occurred in 1475 patients in the rivaroxaban group (14.9% per year) and in 1449 in the warfarin group (14.5% per year) (hazard ratio, 1.03; 95% CI, 0.96 to 1.11; P = 0.44)

major_points.text: Intracranial hemorrhage and fatal bleeding were significantly less frequent with rivaroxaban than warfarin.
major_points.quote: with significant reductions in intracranial hemorrhage (0.5% vs. 0.7%, P = 0.02) and fatal bleeding (0.2% vs. 0.5%, P = 0.003) in the rivaroxaban group.

inclusion_criteria.text: Nonvalvular atrial fibrillation documented on electrocardiography.
inclusion_criteria.quote: We recruited patients with nonvalvular atrial fibril- lation, as documented on electrocardiography, who were at moderate-to-high risk for stroke.

inclusion_criteria.text: Elevated stroke risk indicated by history of stroke, transient ischemic attack, or systemic embolism, or at least two specified risk factors (heart failure/LVEF ≤35%, hypertension, age ≥75, or diabetes).
inclusion_criteria.quote: Elevated risk was indicated by a history of stroke, transient ischemic attack, or systemic embolism or at least two of the following risk factors: heart failure or a left ventricular ejection fraction of 35% or less, hypertension, an age of 75 years or more, or the presence of diabetes mellitus
presence of diabetes mellitus (i.e., a CHADS2 score of 2 or more, on a scale ranging from 1 to 6, with higher scores indicating a greater risk of stroke).

criticisms.text: One site had Good Clinical Practice guideline violations making data unreliable; 93 patients were excluded from all efficacy analyses before unblinding.
criticisms.quote: Because of violations in Good Clinical Prac- tice guidelines at one site that made the data un- reliable, 93 patients (50 in the rivaroxaban group and 43 in the warfarin group) were excluded from all efficacy analyses before unblinding.

criticisms.text: Premature permanent cessation of randomized treatment was slightly higher than in other studies.
criticisms.quote: the rate of premature, permanent cessation of randomized treatment (14.3% in year 1) was slightly higher than in other studies (average, 11%).
